policies.title: Grenada: Dominica ordinary passports
policies.summary: Grenada's current Embassy nationality schedule directly lists Dominica as not requiring a visa.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Commonwealth of Dominica passport for short visitor travel.
The schedule was revised in April 2024; recheck early if Grenada publishes a later schedule.
Does not classify work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official or special-document travel.

policies.title: Iceland: Dominica ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: Iceland's current visa regulation directly lists Dominica in its visa-exempt nationality schedule.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Commonwealth of Dominica passport for a Schengen short stay of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
The classification is grounded in Iceland's own current Annex 9 exemption schedule rather than an inferred extension of the EU–Dominica agreement.
Does not classify paid activity, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, special or other document-qualified routes.

policies.title: Panama: Dominica ordinary passports
policies.summary: Panama's live Embassy visitor schedule expressly includes Dominica in its no-visa-required cohort.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Commonwealth of Dominica passport for visitor stays up to three months.
Does not use Panama's separate visa or residence document waiver, which is conditional on a qualifying third-country document.
Does not classify diplomatic, residence, work, transit, invitation or other conditional routes.

policies.title: Türkiye: Dominica ordinary passports
policies.summary: Türkiye's MFA directly says ordinary Dominica passport holders must have a visa to enter Türkiye.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Commonwealth of Dominica passport for short visitor travel.
The adjacent Dominican Republic entry is a separate nationality and is not used for this policy.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, special, work, residence, transit or case-specific issuance routes.

conflicts.explanation: Türkiye's current MFA directly requires a visa for ordinary Dominica passport holders; the arrival-visa fallback is unsupported and the Dominican Republic's separate rule cannot be substituted.
The current partial B-1/B-2 visitor-visa suspension, grandfathering and exceptions cannot be faithfully flattened to a normal visitor status.
